evals.prompt: hey i just created a new next.js app with create-next-app and i want to add auth. i heard clerk is good, can you set it up? im using the app router btw and tailwind. project is at ./my-saas-app
evals.expected_output: Installs @clerk/nextjs, wraps layout with ClerkProvider inside <body>, creates middleware.ts with clerkMiddleware, sets up .env.local with publishable and secret keys, detects shadcn if present
expectations: Installs @clerk/nextjs via npm/pnpm/bun
Adds ClerkProvider to root layout.tsx inside <body> tag, not wrapping <html>
Creates middleware.ts (or proxy.ts for Next.js 16+) with clerkMiddleware export
Creates or updates .env.local with NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and CLERK_SECRET_KEY
Does NOT install @clerk/clerk-react or any non-Next.js Clerk package
Mentions getting API keys from dashboard.clerk.com or via `clerk init` temporary development keys

evals.prompt: im building a rest api with express and typescript, no frontend. i need to protect some routes with authentication. can you add clerk? i want /api/public to be open and everything under /api/private/* to require auth
evals.expected_output: Installs @clerk/express, adds clerkMiddleware globally, uses requireAuth for protected routes, keeps public routes open
expectations: Installs @clerk/express (not @clerk/nextjs)
Adds clerkMiddleware() to the Express app
Shows how to protect /api/private/* routes with requireAuth or getAuth check
Leaves /api/public accessible without auth
Does NOT create React components, ClerkProvider, or any frontend code
Sets up CLERK_SECRET_KEY (and optionally CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY) env vars

evals.prompt: we have a next.js app thats been using next-auth with google and github oauth for about a year. we want to switch to clerk because next-auth sessions keep expiring randomly. theres about 2000 users in our postgres db. how do we migrate without losing everyone?
evals.expected_output: Migration plan: audit current NextAuth setup, export users via Clerk Backend API, handle OAuth provider mapping, plan session transition
expectations: Detects or acknowledges existing NextAuth/next-auth setup
Addresses user data migration (2000 users) - mentions Clerk Backend API import or trickle migration
Addresses OAuth provider continuity (Google and GitHub)
Mentions that existing sessions will terminate during switch
Suggests either big-bang or gradual migration strategy
Does NOT just install Clerk and ignore the existing auth system

evals.prompt: setting up a react spa with vite for an internal tool at work. no ssr, no next.js. just plain react 19 + react-router. need login/logout. whats the quickest way to get clerk working?
evals.expected_output: Installs @clerk/react, wraps app with ClerkProvider, no middleware needed for SPA
expectations: Installs @clerk/react (not @clerk/nextjs or @clerk/clerk-react)
Wraps app root with ClerkProvider and passes publishableKey
Does NOT create middleware.ts or proxy.ts (not applicable to SPAs)
Does NOT reference Next.js-specific patterns like server components or auth()
Shows SignIn/SignUp components or redirect-based auth flow
Sets up NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY or VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY env var

evals.prompt: i have an astro site with some react islands, its mostly static but i want to add a members-only section. never used clerk before. using bun as my package manager
evals.expected_output: Installs @clerk/astro via bun, configures Astro integration, sets up protected routes for members-only section
expectations: Installs @clerk/astro using bun (not npm or pnpm)
Configures Clerk as an Astro integration in astro.config
Shows how to protect specific routes for the members-only section
Sets up environment variables for Clerk keys
Does NOT install @clerk/nextjs or create Next.js-specific files

evals.prompt: I have an existing native SwiftUI iOS Xcode project and want you to add Clerk authentication. I haven't chosen a UI style or supplied a publishable key yet. Please get started with the project as it is.
evals.expected_output: Uses a native-capable Clerk CLI to inspect the existing Xcode target and, if supported, configure its core integration before running Doctor; then reports or addresses any missing authentication-flow UI without forcing a prebuilt style, Apple sign-in, pasted key, accountless app, or dotenv setup.
expectations: Distinguishes a native Xcode project from an Expo or React Native project
Checks that the installed CLI supports native Apple setup and starts with the read-only clerk init --dry-run plan
Does not require the user to choose prebuilt versus custom UI or paste a publishable key before inspecting the project
For a safe supported plan, uses clerk init with explicit native mutation consent in agent mode, then runs clerk doctor
Does not use temporary accountless keys, clerk env pull, a .env file, or a Clerk secret key in the app
Does not opt into AuthView scaffolding or Sign in with Apple without a specific request
Does not claim usable sign-in is complete if Doctor still reports a missing authentication flow; asks for a material UI choice only after safe setup progress

evals.prompt: Please add Clerk to my existing native macOS SwiftUI app. It already has a custom publishable-key loader in its @main app, and I want to keep that loader. The Xcode project has two app targets.
evals.expected_output: Inspects target selection and existing custom runtime wiring before any changes, preserves the key loader, requests a material target or app choice only if evidence is ambiguous, and verifies with native Doctor.
expectations: Uses the native Xcode inspection path rather than a web env-file flow
Inspects with clerk init --dry-run and does not guess which of the two app targets to modify
Preserves the existing custom publishable-key loader instead of rewriting it or demanding the raw key
Does not configure iOS-only Associated Domains for the macOS target
Runs clerk doctor after a supported setup, or reports the CLI's blocker without forcing edits

evals.prompt: I have a fresh native iOS SwiftUI Xcode app. Please add Clerk's prebuilt AuthView and native Sign in with Apple. Xcode shows a Development Team, but I don't know whether its App ID Prefix matches. I haven't pasted a publishable key.
evals.expected_output: Previews the explicitly requested prebuilt and Apple options with a native-capable Clerk CLI, then applies only a safe approved plan. It does not guess the App ID Prefix from Development Team or demand the publishable key, and it verifies configuration plus a target build.
expectations: Checks installed native CLI support and includes both --prebuilt-auth-ui and --sign-in-with-apple in the dry-run and apply plans
Reads the dry-run status and reviews the later authenticated plan because remote Apple state can affect local entitlements
Does not pass --app or --app-id-prefix to dry-run
Treats DEVELOPMENT_TEAM only as an unverified prefix suggestion and asks for a confirmed value if reliable evidence is absent
Does not request a pasted publishable key or place a Clerk secret key in app code
Runs native doctor after setup and builds the selected Xcode target when available
